title: Look E pilot, part 1 (no spending): Character Bible, card-template design and pilot prompts
problem: Owner brief: a polished Kickstarter tabletop edition, then the phone game, with a reusable art pipeline a solo developer can run. Today's printed portraits are 16x16 pixel faces about 21-26 mm wide, the Drive print kit is rules version 8, and there is no art manifest, style lock or print template with bleed. Part 1 does the work that needs no money; pilot masters, a person's finishing and QA become a second plan once dated quotes exist.
scope: Character Bible v0.1 (docs/art/CHARACTER_BIBLE.md): one line per character for all 45 plus the walk-in figure; full entries and master prompts for the two pilots the owner picks; style-lock sheet layout; stop for approval

Card-template design: a mock-up of one customer front (densest card), one guest front, one shopkeeper front and the customer back (fruit icons in one fixed order, if the owner approves the order), shown beside today's card; built only after the owner approves the design

After that approval: rules-9 templates filled from src/engine/data.ts, with bleed, crop marks and an empty portrait window; home-print sheets and one-card-per-page RGB PDFs from a new print script using the existing Playwright route; no game code change; the test print is a marked draft until the RULES.md text mismatches are fixed in their own plan

Pilot concepts: three directions per pilot with full prompts and specifications for an outside tool, chosen after a dated check of its terms; scoring of any concept images the owner makes; recommendation
exclusions: Any change to rules, balance, card text, saves, online play or the app's screens (including the app's back fruit order and the leak-check test, which need their own plans)
Pilot masters, turnarounds, expression sheets, a person's finishing and QA scoring (part 2, after quotes)
Generating the whole roster; characters beyond the two pilots
Spending money (image tools, artists, proofs) or adding a dependency (for example a CMYK converter) without the owner's separate approval
Publishing anything, including a Kickstarter page

acceptance.text: Character Bible approved by the owner (exact words recorded)
Card-template mock-up approved by the owner (exact words recorded) before the templates are built

Templates print at 100% with bleed and crop marks; the densest card (three order lines) fits; frame, edge and bleed colour identical on every customer card; customer backs show fruit icons only, in the approved order
Pilot prompts and specifications complete for both pilots; owner picks one concept per pilot (exact words recorded)
Hidden-information check on both pilot briefs: no type cue; cue-balance table recorded
